Wait, but the state graph tracks states, not just actions. If I'm in a different state now (after the clockwise rotation), then counter-clockwise from this state should be untried. Unless the clockwise rotation brought me back to the same state as before the counter-clockwise rotation.
Let me think... The initial state had the perimeter as w g S b p Y g p b S g p S b b w w g p S. After 1 counter-clockwise rotation, it would be g S b p Y g p b S g p S b b w w g p S w. Let me try rotating clockwise multiple times to explore all 20 states. But the no_impact check stopped my batch of 5 counter-clockwise rotations. Let me try a single clockwise rotation first.
Wait, but I already tried clockwise rotation from this state (it's the same as the initial state). So it's also a known action.
Hmm, so from the initial state, I've tried both clockwise and counter-clockwise rotations. Both lead to states I've already visited (since rotating one way and then the other brings me back).
So the state graph has 2 nodes: the initial state and the state after 1 counter-clockwise rotation. From the initial state, I've tried both clockwise and counter-clockwise. From the other state, I've tried clockwise (which brings me back to initial).
Wait, that means I've explored the entire state graph for rotations! There are only 2 states reachable by rotation, and I've tried both actions from both states. But the level isn't complete.
